question: What is the bacterium that causes syphilis?
explanation: Syphilis is a systemic infection caused by the spirochete bacterium Treponema pallidum. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h1)

question: At what point in pregnancy can the syphilis bacterium cross the placenta to infect the fetus?

options.A: Only during active labor and vaginal delivery
options.B: Only after the infant has taken its first breath
options.C: Exclusively in the final weeks of the third trimester
options.D: As early as the first trimester around the ninth week

explanation: Treponema pallidum can cross the placenta to infect the fetus as early as the ninth week of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which sign is most characteristic of primary syphilis?

options.A: Painful fluid-filled blisters on the vulva
options.B: High fever and severe lower abdominal pain
options.C: A widespread rash on the palms and soles
options.D: A single, painless ulcer called a chancre

explanation: The hallmark sign of primary syphilis is a painless sore known as a chancre at the infection site. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which symptom commonly appears during the secondary stage of syphilis?

options.A: Yellowish vaginal discharge with a strong fishy odor
options.B: Sudden paralysis of the lower limbs and severe headache
options.C: Large, painful boils spreading across the abdomen
options.D: A non-itchy rash on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet

explanation: Secondary syphilis typically presents with a distinctive rash that affects the palms and soles, alongside swollen lymph nodes. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which blood tests are commonly used as initial screening tools for syphilis in antenatal clinics?
explanation: VDRL and RPR are standard screening tests used to detect active syphilis infection and monitor treatment response. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is a positive treponemal test result alone not enough to prove a patient has an active, current infection?

options.A: Treponemal antibodies disappear within two weeks of contracting the disease
options.B: Treponemal antibodies usually remain in the blood for life, even after successful treatment
options.C: Treponemal tests frequently give false-positive results in healthy pregnant women
options.D: Treponemal tests only measure acute inflammation rather than the presence of bacteria

explanation: Because treponemal antibodies persist long-term regardless of whether the infection is active or cured, these tests cannot differentiate past treated infections from current ones. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the preferred medication for treating syphilis during pregnancy?
explanation: Benzathine Penicillin G is the standard treatment capable of treating the pregnant woman and curing the fetal infection. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h4)

question: What causes a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction shortly after a patient receives her first penicillin injection for syphilis?

options.A: A sudden spike in blood pressure caused by the injection technique
options.B: A severe immediate allergic reaction to the penicillin molecule
options.C: Secondary bacterial infection invading healing ulcers
options.D: The sudden destruction of spirochetes releasing toxins into the bloodstream

explanation: The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction is an inflammatory response triggered by the rapid release of byproducts when a large number of treponemal bacteria are destroyed at once. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which clinical manifestation in a newborn is commonly referred to as 'snuffles' in congenital syphilis?

options.A: A persistent, highly infectious nasal discharge
options.B: Severe nasal congestion caused by dry crusts
options.C: A wet, hacking cough accompanied by wheezing
options.D: Rapid, shallow breathing due to pneumonia

explanation: Snuffles is an early sign of congenital syphilis, presenting as a copious, infectious nasal discharge that resembles a severe cold. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h5)

question: To help prevent congenital syphilis, when must maternal treatment be completed before delivery?

options.A: Within 48 hours of onset of labor
options.B: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.C: By the end of the first trimester

explanation: Maternal treatment must be completed at least 30 days prior to delivery to ensure adequate treatment of the fetus. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why is treating the sexual partner of a pregnant woman diagnosed with syphilis just as important as treating the woman?

options.A: To satisfy mandatory legal requirements for marriage counseling
options.B: To prevent reinfection of the pregnant woman during the same gestation
options.C: To prevent the partner from developing tertiary syphilis symptoms
options.D: To ensure the partner's blood type is compatible with the baby

explanation: If sexual partners are left untreated, they will continually re-expose the pregnant woman to the infection, neutralizing the benefits of her treatment. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h6)

question: A pregnant woman tests positive for syphilis at her 28-week visit and receives treatment. What is the most critical next step for the midwife regarding her partner?

options.A: Wait until the postnatal period before advising the partner to visit the clinic
options.B: Instruct the partner to come in for immediate blood testing and simultaneous treatment
options.C: Prescribe prophylactic antibiotics for the partner without testing him first
options.D: Advise the couple to abstain from sex completely until the baby is delivered

explanation: Partner notification and concurrent treatment are essential steps to halt the cycle of infection and prevent maternal reinfection. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h6)
